The diagnostic skill: tells you what's happened on a ticket, what hasn't, and what the next valid action is. Useful at any point in the workflow.

## Layout

```text
skills/audit-ticket-process/
├── SKILL.md
├── README.qmd
├── install.sh
└── scripts/
    └── audit_ticket_process.py
```

## Install

```bash
bash skills/audit-ticket-process/install.sh
```

## Usage through Claude

> "Where are we on TKT-00042?"

Claude reads `SKILL.md`, runs the script, and reports the state + recommended next skill.

## Direct CLI

```bash
uv run python skills/audit-ticket-process/scripts/audit_ticket_process.py --ticket-id TKT-00042
```

The script prints a state, a chronological timeline, workflow flags, and the recommended next action. It also appends an audit row to `data/working/ticket_action_log.csv`.

## Public functions

- `load_ticket_history(data_dir, out_dir, ticket_id)` — pulls every relevant row across raw, processed, and working CSVs.
- `infer_current_state(history)` — returns `{state, flags}`. State is one of `submitted_awaiting_triage`, `triaged_awaiting_faq_check`, `faq_checked_awaiting_decision`, `escalated_awaiting_specialist`, `specialist_solution_ready_for_relay`, `response_sent_awaiting_customer`, `feedback_recorded_action_pending`, `closed`.
- `list_valid_next_actions(state)` — maps state → recommended skill name(s).
- `build_audit_report(history, state)` — full printable report.
- `main(argv)` — CLI. Exits 2 on missing ticket / data, 0 on success regardless of the state (audit always succeeds when the ticket exists).

## Working vs historical

Working data (`data/working/*.csv`) is the live skill output. Processed data (`data/processed/*.csv`) is the synthetic historical log. The audit prefers working rows when picking the current state but always shows historical rows in the timeline as `(historical)` so demos against pre-existing tickets still tell a complete story.

## Test

```bash
uv run pytest tests/skills/test_audit_ticket_process.py -v
```
